messages:
Maya Chen: Hey folks — quick Q about adding my domestic partner to medical + dental. I started last week (effective 2024-04-17). The benefits portal shows a dependent flow but the dropdown only lists spouse/child. Do we need extra paperwork for domestic partners? Also wondering about effective date and payroll deductions. Thanks!

Jordan (People Ops): Welcome again, Maya! You can add a domestic partner — we require a signed domestic partner affidavit plus one proof of shared residence (lease, joint bank stmt, utility). I can DM the PDF form. If you want the coverage effective from your start date (4/17) we need docs within the 30-day window and before the payroll cutoff for the next cycle — carrier rules can vary. Adding @Samira (Benefits) to confirm carrier specifics.

Samira (Benefits): Hi Maya — yep, we handle domestic partners. Docs we need: domestic partner affidavit (signed by both parties) + one proof of cohabitation dated within the last 90 days. Send to benefits@redwood.com. If you submit within 30 days we can make the effective date retroactive to your start date. If you need the earliest possible effective date, put "RETRO" in the email subject so we prioritize.

Maya Chen: Thanks — good to know. Quick follow-up: will the payroll deductions be prorated? My first paycheck already processed and only shows base pay (no benefits deductions). Should I expect a big deduction next pay or something spread out?

Jordan (People Ops): @PayrollBot can you confirm the proration behavior for mid-cycle enrollments and retro effective dates?

PayrollBot: PayrollBot: For mid-cycle enrollments submitted after payroll cutoff, deductions are applied starting next pay period. If carrier allows a retro effective date to the start of employment and we process retro, payroll will attempt to calculate a prorated deduction to capture the earlier coverage period (subject to payroll cutoff and carrier chargeback rules). If carrier requires billing directly, benefits team will coordinate.

Samira (Benefits): To add: HSA elections are separate — if you're electing HSA, make the election in Workday within 30 days or contributions default to 0. HSA contributions are taken per paycheck, so if we need to catch up, we can set a prorated per-paycheck amount for the rest of the year on request.

Maya Chen: One more complication — my partner currently has COBRA from their old job and the COBRA notice expires 2024-05-10. If we enroll them here, will there be any gap or issues with terminating COBRA? Should I wait until COBRA ends or enroll now?

Jordan (People Ops): If the effective date here is before the COBRA end date, COBRA can be declined. Best practice: enroll here with your preferred effective date, then send COBRA termination docs to the COBRA administrator showing the new coverage. Samira, any carrier-specific tips on avoiding double-billing?

Samira (Benefits): Practical approach: enroll now and set desired effective date (we can do retro to 4/17). After we confirm coverage with the carrier, email benefits@redwood.com with "COBRA" in the subject and attach COBRA paperwork. We'll coordinate with the COBRA admin to stop billing. If the carrier enforces overlap billing, we will help submit for reimbursement/adjustment, but timely paperwork avoids most issues.

Maya Chen: Great — uploading affidavit + lease as proof to benefits@redwood.com now. I included "RETRO + COBRA" in the subject. Thanks for the clear steps!

Samira (Benefits): Got the upload, thanks Maya. We'll confirm receipt and follow up if anything is missing. Aiming to process for a 2024-04-17 effective date. :thumbsup:

Jordan (People Ops): Thanks — filing a note on payroll's side so they watch for the retro request. If anything else pops up just ping this thread or DM me.

Maya Chen: Appreciate it, everyone!
